summary: K. R. Norman worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Taunton School and Downing College, Cambridge, under Harold Walter Bailey. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (1955–1992) and edited the PTS Journal (1981–1994).
K. S. Balasubramanian is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He served at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Jean Philippe Vogel. He taught Pāli at Leiden University (1948–1963) and was a professor at the University of Amsterdam (1960–1981).
K. Sambasiva Sastri was an Indologist who served as Curator at the Department of Oriental Manuscripts Publications from circa 1923 to 1934, succeeding T. Ganapati Sastri.

K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College. He also held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

Working in Buddhist studies and archaeology, Koshalee earned degrees and diplomas from the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Archaeology, among other institutions. Academic appointments include posts at Kelaniya, the University of Ruhuna, and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

K. V. Puttappa was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore between circa 1925 and 1929.

K. V. Raman specialized in archaeology and Indology, studying at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Institute of Archaeology. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1957–1976) and at the University of Madras.

K. V. Ramesh was a scholar in Indology and archaeology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987), and Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).

K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar worked in the fields of Indology and history and archaeology. His main appointments included serving as Principal of Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College from circa 1935 to 1940.

K. Venkata Ramanan studied Buddhist studies and philosophy under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang at Peking University, and under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi at Visva-Bharati University, where he received a Doctor of Letters and taught. He also visited the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

K. de B. Codrington was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Corpus Christi College and Wadham College. He held professorships at the University of Cincinnati and SOAS University of London, and served as Keeper of the Indian Section at the Victoria and Albert Museum.

Kaetan Andreevich Kossovich worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Aleksej Stepanovič Homjakov and at Moscow State University. His career included teaching at Tver Gymnasium, editing at the National Library of Russia, and a professorship at Saint Petersburg State University.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Kai Donner was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Otto Donner and at the University of Cambridge, later holding a post at the University of Helsinki from circa 1924 to 1935.

Kaie Mochizuki is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. His academic career includes serving as a professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and as president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. He held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho Universities, and served as principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School.

Kaiten Nukariya, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, studied at institutions including Komazawa University and Keio University under Ryodo Nukariya. He lectured at Harvard University (c. 1913–1914) and served as the first president of Komazawa University.
Kaiun Shirodate specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Shirodate held posts at Otani University as a full-time lecturer (attested 1986–1990) and later as a professor (attested 1999–2002).
